summary: TCP/UDP/TLS networking with native stream pumps
lead: TCP/UDP/TLS networking. TCP has three explicit data paths: message APIs (`read` / `write`) expose bytes as strings, buffer APIs (`readInto` / `writeBytes`) reuse caller-owned `Bytes`, and stream APIs (`copy` / `copyBidirectional`) keep payload in native buffers for high-throughput relays.
usage: Usage: `import net` and create typed `NetListener` / `NetConn` handles with `listen`, `accept`, and `dial`.

sections.heading: TCP data paths
sections.markdown: `net.read(conn)` and `net.write(conn, data)` are for message-oriented code that needs to inspect or transform data in Xray. `net.readInto(conn, bytes, maxlen?)` and `net.writeBytes(conn, bytes)` are the reusable-buffer binary path. `net.copy(src, dst)` and `net.copyBidirectional(a, b)` are raw TCP/TLS stream pumps; payload stays in reusable native buffers. Echo is just the self-copy case: `net.copy(conn, conn)`.

sections.heading: Deadlines and errors
sections.markdown: Use `setReadDeadline`, `setWriteDeadline`, `setDeadline`, and `setAcceptDeadline` with `time.monotonic()` deadlines. Operations return the normal null or `-1` failure shape, and `lastError(handle)` / `lastErrno(handle)` expose diagnostic causes such as `timeout`, `closed`, `reset`, `refused`, `dns`, `tls`, and `io`.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
sections.markdown: `shutdownRead`, `shutdownWrite`, and `shutdown` expose TCP half-close semantics. `copyBidirectional(a, b)` runs two stream pumps and half-closes the opposite write side on EOF, which is the preferred primitive for generic TCP proxy and relay code.

sections.heading: Echo server
Design rule
bullets: Use typed handles (`NetConn`, `NetListener`) instead of ad-hoc JSON handles.
Use stream pumps for proxy, relay, echo, and other byte-preserving workloads.
Use `Bytes` buffers for binary protocol hot paths that must inspect payload.
Use string reads only when the program actually needs to parse or mutate text.
